narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story and introduces each speech.

the-lord.name: The Lord
the-lord.note: God, answering Job out of the whirlwind and judging the friends.

1.t: Then the Lord answered Job out of a whirlwind, and said:

2.t: Who is this that wrappeth up sentences in unskilful words?

3.t: Gird up thy loins like a man: I will ask thee, and answer thou me.

4.t: Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth? tell me if thou hast understanding.

5.t: Who hath laid the measures thereof, if thou knowest or who hath stretched the line upon it?

6.t: Upon what are its bases grounded? or who laid the corner stone thereof,

7.t: When the morning stars praised me together, and all the sons of God made a joyful melody?

8.t: Who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke forth as issuing out of the womb:

9.t: When I made a cloud the garment thereof, and wrapped it in a mist as in swaddling bands?

10.t: I set my bounds around it, and made it bars and doors:

11.t: And I said: Hitherto thou shalt come, and shalt go no further, and here thou shalt break thy swelling waves.

12.t: Didst thou since thy birth command the morning, and shew the dawning of the day its place?

13.t: And didst thou hold the extremities of the earth shaking them, and hast thou shaken the ungodly out of it?

14.t: The seal shall be restored as clay, and shall stand as a garment.

15.t: From the wicked their light shall be taken away, and the high arm shall be broken.

16.t: Hast thou entered into the depths of the sea, and walked in the lowest parts of the deep?

17.t: Have the gates of death been opened to thee, and hast thou seen the darksome doors?

18.t: Hast thou considered the breadth of the earth? tell me, if thou knowest all things?

19.t: Where is the way where light dwelleth, and where is the place of darkness?

20.t: That thou mayst bring every thing to its own bounds, and understand the paths of the house thereof.

21.t: Didst thou know then that thou shouldst be born? and didst thou know the number of thy days?

22.t: Hast thou entered into the storehouses of the snow, or hast thou beheld the treasures of the hail:

23.t: Which I have prepared for the time of the enemy, against the day of battle and war?

24.t: By what way is the light spread, and heat divided upon the earth?

25.t: Who gave a course to violent showers, or a way for noisy thunder:

26.t: That it should rain on the earth without man in the wilderness, where no mortal dwelleth:

27.t: That it should fill the desert and desolate land, and should bring forth green grass?

28.t: Who is the father of rain? or who begot the drops of dew?

29.t: Out of whose womb came the ice? and the frost from heaven who hath gendered it?

30.t: The waters are hardened like a stone, and the surface of the deep is congealed.

31.t: Shalt thou be able to join together the shining stars the Pleiades, or canst thou stop the turning about of Arcturus?

32.t: Canst thou bring forth the day star in its time, and make the evening star to rise upon the children of the earth?

33.t: Dost thou know the order of heaven, and canst thou set down the reason thereof on the earth?

34.t: Canst thou lift up thy voice to the clouds, that an abundance of waters may cover thee?

35.t: Canst thou send lightnings, and will they go, and will they return and say to thee: Here we are?

36.t: Who hath put wisdom in the heart of man? or who gave the cock understanding?

37.t: Who can declare the order of the heavens, or who can make the harmony of heaven to sleep?

38.t: When was the dust poured on the earth, and the clods fastened together?

39.t: Wilt thou take the prey for the lioness, and satisfy the appetite of her whelps,

40.t: When they couch in the dens and lie in wait in holes?

41.t: Who provideth food for the raven, when her young ones cry to God, wandering about, because they have no meat?
